extracted.intended_audience: covered entities (health programs and activities), compliance officers, legal counsel, and health care administrators responsible for Section 1557 compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for covered entities on implementing Section 1557-required policies and procedures, including language access procedures, effective communication procedures, reasonable modification procedures, employee training, and notices of nondiscrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language Access Procedures (§92.8(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must develop, implement, and maintain language access procedures that meaningfully provide language assistance to individuals with limited English proficiency (LEP). Procedures should identify preferred language assistance services providers and determine which providers can accommodate the non-English languages most spoken in the service area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance and examples from the preamble: covered entities should analyze language needs in the service area (e.g., identify most spoken non-English languages) and confirm interpreter/translation providers can meet those needs. Covered entities with existing language access plans are encouraged to sustain and modify them to include required elements; if an existing plan meets §92.8(d), a separate procedures document is not required. OCR will make sample procedures available on www.hhs.gov/1557 but will not endorse private providers. Entities should reference HHS LEP Guidance (68 FR 47313-22), lep.gov language-access-planning resources, and HHS's 2023 Language Access Plan for further planning guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directory of Qualified Bilingual/Multilingual Staff (element of §92.8(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Language access procedures must include a current list (directory) of qualified bilingual/multilingual staff members so employees can identify such staff quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR acknowledges employee turnover but declines to remove the requirement. Covered entities should periodically revise procedures to reflect staffing changes. The directory is intended to facilitate timely delivery of language assistance. If a covered entity delegates language service access to a department or functional group, contact information for that department or group should be included in the procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translated Materials Access (element of §92.8(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Language access procedures must include how to access electronic translations (i.e., location on network, intranet, or external-facing website) and include the date of issuance for translated materials (replacing 'publication date'). The rule no longer requires listing the physical location of written translated materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR revised the proposal to remove the burden of maintaining locations of all written translated materials; instead require instructions for accessing electronic translations. Use 'date of issuance' to account for hard copy or electronic formats. Maintain a current list of translated materials (electronic access information and issuance date) to serve timely and effective language assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Communication Procedures (§92.8(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must develop effective communication procedures to ensure effective communication with individuals with disabilities across modalities. Procedures must equip employees with information and tools necessary to meet communication needs for many types of disabilities (sensory, manual, speaking, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures may include how to determine the sign language an individual uses, whether interpreter teams (e.g., certified deaf interpreter plus ASL interpreter) are needed, and other auxiliary aids and services beyond qualified interpreters. Covered entities may use existing communication access plans in place of a separate procedures document if they meet §92.8(e). Although OCR agrees effective communication and language access are interdependent and ideally coordinated, it declined to impose additional regulatory provisions requiring such coordination because such standards would be difficult to objectively measure. OCR also declined to require inclusion in procedures of how entities will assess staff competency as interpreters/readers because assessment flexibility is addressed in §92.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable Modification Procedures (§92.8(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must implement written procedures describing how an individual may request a reasonable modification, and how the covered entity processes, evaluates, and responds to such requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR intends the requirement to raise awareness and compliance. Reasonable modifications are not exhaustively listed, but include changes in modality of communication (e.g., email instead of phone), scheduling accommodations (e.g., afternoon appointments), and telehealth in place of in-person when not a fundamental alteration. A covered entity must sometimes provide modifications without an affirmative request when it has knowledge of the individual's disability or the need is obvious. OCR recommends documenting reasonable modification requests in medical records as a best practice to avoid repeated requests by patients, but declines to make documentation prescriptive. The Section 1557 Coordinator (required for entities with 15+ employees under §92.7) is responsible for ensuring compliance; OCR declines to require designation of an additional employee solely for reasonable modifications. OCR retains the established legal term 'reasonable modification' and declines to change it to 'reasonable and appropriate.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on Section 1557 Policies and Procedures (§92.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must train relevant employees of their health programs and activities on the entity's tailored Section 1557 Policies and Procedures, document completion of training, and retain training documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key elements and clarifications: (a) Timing — covered entities must begin training relevant employees no later than 30 days after implementing their policies and procedures and no later than 300 days after the effective date of the part; new employees must be trained within a reasonable period after hire; employees whose roles are affected by material changes must be retrained. (b) Documentation — entities must contemporaneously document completion in written or electronic form and retain those records for no less than three calendar years (regulatory text modified to 'retain' training documentation for the requisite period). (c) Definition — 'relevant employees' for §92.9 includes permanent and temporary employees whose roles entail interacting with patients/public; making decisions that affect patient care (including executive leadership and legal counsel); or performing tasks affecting patients' financial obligations (billing/collections). (d) Content and format — training must be based on the covered entity's own policies and procedures; OCR provides supplemental resources at www.hhs.gov/1557 but will not prescribe overly specific training curricula. Entities may incorporate Section 1557 training into existing compliance training or make it standalone; OCR encourages methods that maximize knowledge retention (interactive formats). (e) Transferability — training completion for one covered entity is not transferable to another because policies/procedures are entity-specific. OCR will not exempt specific specialties from the training requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Nondiscrimination (§92.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must provide a Notice of Nondiscrimination relating to their health programs and activities to participants, beneficiaries, enrollees, applicants, and members of the public, with required contents set out in the regulatory text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A covered entity may combine the Section 1557 Notice of Nondiscrimination with notices required by Title VI, §504, Title IX, and the Age Act, provided the combined notice clearly informs individuals of their civil rights under Section 1557 and meets the content requirements of §92.10(a)(1). OCR sought comment on accessibility of the notice to individuals with disabilities and individuals with LEP; entities should consider accessible formats and language access when providing the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility and Use of Existing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities that already have language access plans or communication access plans may modify those plans to include required elements of §92.8(d) and §92.8(e); where an existing plan meets the regulatory requirements, a separate procedures document is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR encourages advance planning as essential to compliance but does not explicitly require advance planning; entities are permitted to include more information than required and to adapt existing plans. This flexibility also extends to how entities assess interpreter qualifications (see §92.4) and how they design trainings, within the requirement that training be tailored to the entity's own policies and procedures.
